claims.text: Trafalgar Square is Central London's main public square and is widely known as a center for national celebrations and political demonstrations.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The square was named to commemorate the Battle of Trafalgar, a famous British naval victory over France and Spain on 21 October 1805.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Interestingly, the name 'Trafalgar' itself is a Spanish word of Arabic origin, derived from phrases meaning 'cape of the cave' or 'extremity of the west'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Before becoming a public square, the site was occupied by the King's Mews, where royal hawks and later horses were kept from the 13th century until they were moved to Buckingham Palace.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In the late 1950s, building work surprisingly uncovered prehistoric fossils on the site, revealing that cave lions, rhinoceroses, and hippopotamuses once roamed the area.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: At the center of the square stands the 169-foot Nelson's Column, which is surrounded by four bronze lions and commemorates Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The square is famous for its 'fourth plinth', which was originally intended for an equestrian statue but has instead hosted a rotating display of contemporary artworks since 1999.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Every year since 1947, the government of Norway has generously donated a large Christmas tree to be erected in the square for the holidays.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The square used to be famously overrun by hundreds of feral pigeons, but their population was drastically reduced after a 2003 bylaw made it illegal to feed them.
claims.subject: self
